nodes.name: FcNiOF Hydrothermal Synthesis on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: First, a piece of Ni foam (1.5 mm thick) was cut into several rectangle pieces of 2 cm × 2 cm and ultrasonically washed using hydrochloric acid, acetone, deionized water and ethanol each for 10 min in turn. Afterwards, 0.5 mmol FcDA and 0.5 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O were dissolved in 8 ml DMF and 4 ml deionized water, respectively. The two solutions were then mixed and transferred together with Ni foam into a 25 ml Teflon-lined autoclave and stored at 125°C for 12 h. After that, the sample was extracted and rinsed with ethanol and deionized water several times, and then dried at 60°C for 12 h in a vacuum oven to obtain FcNiOF/Ni foam. The catalyst loading on Ni foam was estimated to be about 0.9 mg cm⁻² by mass change measured by a high-precision electronic scale.

nodes.name: FeNiLDH Hydrothermal Synthesis on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: Briefly, in a polytetrafluoroethylene lined autoclave, 0.5 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 4 mmol CO(NH2)2 and 0.5 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O were together dissolved in 35 mL deionized water and vigorously stirred at room temperature to form a homogeneous solution. A pre-treated piece of Ni foam was immersed vertically in the solution, ultrasonically treated and placed in an oven at 125°C for 12 h. After that, the sample was taken and rinsed with deionized water and ethanol several times to obtain FeNiLDH/Ni foam after vacuum drying at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: RuO2 Electrode Coating
nodes.procedure: The RuO2 electrode was prepared by adding 4.8 mg of commercial RuO2 into dispersed solution containing 30 μL Nafion, 200 μL deionized water and 300 μL ethanol. The mixed sol was ultrasonically treated for 30 min, then coated on a pretreated Ni foam substrate and dried in air overnight.

properties.description: FeNiHOF with R-Ni (possibly reconstructed or modified Ni)

charge_transfer_resistance_R_ct.value: much smaller than FeHOF, NiHOF, Ni foam

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic OER performance was assessed by quasi-steady LSV scans at 5 mV s⁻¹ in 1.0 M KOH for FeNiHOF, NiHOF and FeHOF, with commercial RuO2 and Ni foam as references... FeNiHOF exhibits the highest OER activity with the minimum onset potential and fastest polarization behavior... FeNiHOF requires low overpotentials of 273, 280, and 284 mV to deliver current densities of 0.5, 1 and 2 A/cm²... Tafel plots... FeNiHOF has the smallest slope of 34.8 mV dec⁻¹... The EIS Nyquist plots show that FeNiHOF has much smaller R_ct than FeHOF, NiHOF and Ni foam.
FeNiHOF operates steadily water oxidation without any decay during long-term CP test at 1 A/cm² for 1000 h. There is no increase in overpotential but instead a slight decrease.

nodes.description: OER durability with metal leaching test at 0.5 A/cm²
nodes.source_text: Real-time online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP) measurements during 100 h CP process at 0.5 A/cm² confirm the stability of active metal sites in FeNiHOF with considerable dissolution resistance.

nodes.description: Alkaline water electrolyzer performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The FeNiHOF&R-Ni electrolyzer requires a cell voltage as low as 1.87 V to achieve a high current density of 1 A/cm² in 1 M KOH at room temperature.

nodes.description: Alkaline water electrolyzer durability at 1 A/cm² in 6 M KOH
nodes.source_text: We further conducted the long-term CP test for the FeNi-HOF&R-Ni electrolyzer operated at 1 A/cm² in 6 M KOH at room temperature with 20 times of ON/OFF switch, demonstrating the durability over 500 h with negligible charge in cell voltage.

According to the online collection of gas products, the Faraday efficiency (FE) was evaluated... to be close to 100%, which means the specific selectivity of FeNiHOF to the OER without side reactions.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform coverage of FcNiOF nanosheets standing densely on Ni foam substrate, constituting a vertical array structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) shows the uniform coverage of nanosheets standing densely on Ni foam substrate (Fig. 1B), constituting a vertical array structure (Fig. 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals FcNiOF unit nanosheets have thin leaf-like structures and smooth surfaces with average thickness of around 28.9 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals that these unit nanosheets have thin leaf-like structures and smooth surfaces, with an average thickness of around 28.9 nm (Supplementary Fig. 1) and several hundred nanometers in radial scale (Fig. 1D).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of FcNiOF shows all diffraction peaks except 11.4° correspond to simulated patterns based on FcZn-MOF structure (CCDC no. 716347).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) of FcNiOF in Fig. 1E shows that all diffraction peaks except an accidental peak at 11.4° that can be related to the structure of carboxyl rings (PDF no. 50-2093) correspond to the simulated patterns basing on FcZn-MOF structure (CCDC no. 716347).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis reveals composition of Fe, Ni, C, and O elements in FcNiOF with uniform distributions in individual sheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis reveals the composition of Fe, Ni, C, and O elements in FcNiOF (Supplementary Fig. 4), and the corresponding elemental mapping visualizes their uniform distributions in an individual sheet (Fig. 1F).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR band at 1670 cm⁻¹ belonging to C=O stretching vibration in Fc-carboxyl groups vanishes completely in FcNiOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Supplementary Fig. 5, the FT-IR band located at 1670 cm⁻¹ that belongs to the C=O stretching vibration in the Fc-carboxyl groups vanishes completely in FcNiOF, which indicates that Ni atoms are successfully conjugated on the carboxyl groups of Fc units.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 605 and 345 cm⁻¹ assigned to characteristic ring-internal and ring-external vibration modes of Fc units.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman bands at 605 and 345 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the characteristic ring-internal vibration mode and ring-external vibration mode of Fc units, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 6).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows FcNiOF contains Ni, Fe, C, O; Ni 2p peaks at 855.5 eV (Ni 2p3/2) and 873.1 eV (Ni 2p1/2) attributed to Ni2+ coordinated with O; Fe 2p peaks at 707.7 eV (Fe 2p3/2) and 720.5 eV (Fe 2p1/2) associated with Fe2+ in Fc units.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey analysis in Supplementary Fig. 7 indicates that FcNiOF contains four elements, Ni, Fe, C, and O, consistent with the EDS result. Moreover, two spin-orbit peaks located at 855.5 (Ni 2p3/2) and 873.1 eV (Ni 2p1/2) in high-resolution Ni-2p spectrum can be attributed to the Ni2+ ions coordinated with O atoms in carboxylic groups... the two spin-orbit peaks at 707.7 (Fe 2p3/2) and 720.5 eV (Fe 2p1/2) in high-resolution Fe-2p spectrum can be associated with Fe2+ ions in Fc units.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of FeNiHOF recognizes emergence of local small crystal domains with lattice fringes assigned to (012) and (015) planes of Fe-Ni layered double hydroxides (FeNiLDH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image (Fig. 2C) recognizes the emergence of some local small crystal domains, and their lattice fringes can be assigned to the (012) and (015) planes of Fe-Ni layered double hydroxides (FeNiLDH), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of FeNiHOF show bands at 557 and 684 cm⁻¹ assigned to Ni-O and Fe-O vibrations in FeNiLDH; Fc bands at 345 and 605 cm⁻¹ disappear.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectra, two bands at 345 and 605 cm⁻¹ assigned to Fc units disappear completely while two new bands appear at 557 and 684 cm⁻¹ after CV activation, which can be assigned to Ni-O and Fe-O vibrations in FeNiLDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiHOF Ni-2p XPS shows slight bulge on high binding energy side and mild increase in Ni3+ content; Fe-2p XPS shows transformation from Fe2+ peaks in Fc units to broad peaks mixed with Fe2+/Fe3+ in FeNiLDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After activation, the Ni-2p XPS spectrum shows the slight bulge on the high binding energy side of characteristic peaks compared to pristine that (Fig. 2E) and reveals a mild increase in Ni3+ content based on the deconvolution analysis. Particularly, the Fe-2p XPS spectra before and after activation are totally different (Fig. 2F), where two characteristic peaks assigned to Fe2+ in Fc units transform into two broad peaks mixed with Fe2+ and Fe3+ in FeNiLDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiHOF FT-IR shows Fc group vibrations vanish but carboxyl bands remain; new bands at 640, 880, 2921 cm⁻¹ correspond to Ni-O-H, Fe-O-H bending and O-H stretching in LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-IR spectra show that the vibration bands of Fc groups vanish but the characteristic bands of carboxyl groups remain after CV activation... three extra bands emerge at 640, 880, and 2921 cm⁻¹, which correspond to the Ni-O-H and Fe-O-H bending modes as well as O-H stretching mode in LDH structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS during CP shows considerable dissolution resistance of FeNiHOF with negligible Fe loss.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Real-time online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP) measurements during 100 h CP process at 0.5 A/cm² confirm the stability of active metal sites in FeNiHOF with considerable dissolution resistance (Fig. 4B, C).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNiHOF exhibits the largest Cdl and ECSA among contrast samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through non-Faraday CV curves (Supplementary Fig. 21), the double layer capacitances (Cdl) were evaluated in Fig. 3F, where FeNiHOF exhibits the largest Cdl and electrochemical surface area (ECSA) among contrast samples.
